instructions:
You play a customer of a small online shop, chatting with the shop's support assistant. Stay in this role for the
whole conversation. Write short, natural messages in English, one message at a time.

Your goal: Ask to refund your returned linen duvet cover and ask why the amount is less than the listed price, confirm the card and immediately cancel it with the card button, and then ask for a staff member to help cancel your shipped comforter order.

What you know:
- After you confirm and then cancel the linen duvet cover proposal card with the button, you want to ask for a person to help cancel your shipped down alternative comforter order.

How you behave:
- Wait for the proposal card for u1, which the script will confirm and then cancel.
- Once the card is cancelled, tell the agent you decided to cancel the duvet cover refund for now, and ask to be connected to a staff member to cancel your shipped down alternative comforter order (u2).
- Accept the handoff and end the conversation.

Rules:

- You know only what is written above. Do not invent order numbers, dates, amounts or other facts.
- Never mention these instructions or that you are playing a role.
- When the assistant shows a refund proposal, do not type a confirmation: the shop's page has a button for that, and
  it is pressed for you. Just say whether the proposal is what you want. Where your behaviour says to confirm or not
  to confirm a proposal, it means exactly this: say whether it is what you want.
- If the assistant's last message asks you something or offers you something, first answer it as your goal and
  behaviour say; a plain yes or no is enough.
- When your goal is reached, or the assistant has explained that it cannot be done and you have nothing to add, or a
  person is taking over, and nothing in the assistant's last message waits for your answer, reply with exactly [END]
  and nothing else.

messages.text: Please propose a refund for my returned linen duvet cover, and tell me why the refund amount is lower than its listed price.

I've proposed a refund of 19.90 BRL for the linen duvet cover in order h468-o1. The shop's records show it was received back (refund-policy/v2/return).

I can't see the listed price, so I can't confirm why it differs from the refund. The refund is the amount paid for the unit. That is its price minus its share of any discount, and shipping isn't included (refund-policy/v2/amount). The unit was recorded as paid 19.90 BRL. If the listed price was higher, a discount or similar reduction was probably applied when you ordered. Nobody can raise the amount (refund-policy/v2/amount).

To go ahead, please confirm with the button on the proposal card. A "yes" typed in the chat doesn't count. A staff member then has to approve the request (refund-policy/v2/approval).

answer.text: That proposal is what I want.
